entries.label: Check: real GDP response to a 0.1% labour productivity rise in all sectors (PC National)
entries.units: % of real GDP per 1% economy-wide labour productivity (long run)

citation.title: National Competition Policy: modelling proposed reforms (study report with appendices)
citation.locator: Table 9, row H1 'Matching', p. 26 (PDF p. 32); Table C.8, row H1a, p. 225 (PDF p. 231)

entries.quote: modelled as an illustrative 0.1% increase … GDP: +$2,646 m (+0.10%) … Modelled shock: Labour productivity is 0.1% higher for all sectors.
entries.derivation: Value = +0.10% of GDP ÷ 0.1% labour productivity = 1.0. Fixed: a check that F-B-01 must reproduce, not a sampled parameter.
entries.notes: The PC's elasticity approach (H1 Matching). A 0.1% fall gives −$2,641m (−0.10%), so the response is symmetric. Aggregate employment is fixed in the long-run closure, so labour productivity and GDP move together (Table D.1, note b).

entries.quote: Table 2: Productivity Measures - Market sector industries aggregate (a) (b) … Two period average income shares … Capital
entries.derivation: Value = the 2024-25 two-period average capital share (0.45). Low and high = its lowest and highest values in the ten years to 2024-25 (0.41 in 2015-16; 0.48 in 2022-23).
entries.notes: A measured statistic (A-P16), as in the plan (§6.2 C3, "market-sector two-period average ≈ 0.45 in 2024-25, Table 2"). Égert and Gal use a standard 0.33 instead (layer-b.alpha.eg2016). The market sector excludes public administration, education and health, so the share may differ for the whole economy.

entries.label: Speed at which MFP closes the gap to its new long-run level (error-correction term)
entries.units: share of the remaining gap closed a year (negative = convergence)

citation.title: The quantification of structural reforms in OECD countries: A new framework
citation.publisher: OECD Economics Department Working Papers No. 1354, ECO/WKP(2016)78
citation.locator: Table 1, row 'error correction term', columns (1)–(3), p. 10 (PDF p. 11); para. 20, p. 14 (PDF p. 15); note to Figure 1, p. 15 (PDF p. 16)

entries.quote: error correction term -0.033** -0.043** -0.052** -0.026** -0.022** … For MFP and capital deepening, the estimated error correction terms are estimated in the range of -0.03 to -0.05
entries.derivation: Value = column (3), the simulation column (−0.052). Low and high = the fastest and slowest of the three MFP columns (−0.052 and −0.033).
entries.notes: The paper's path for year t after a reform of size x is [1 − (1 + ρ)^(t−1)](βx − γx) + γx, where ρ is this term, β the long-run and γ the short-run effect (note to Figure 1, p. 15). The short-run effects are in Table A4.1 (p. 35; ETCR on MFP −0.01 in column 3). A speed of −0.05 means 90% of the convergence takes about 45 years (p. 14, footnote 15).

entries.quote: ETCR (0-6, 6 is strictest) -0.31 0.72% 1.02% 2.09% … Openness (perc. of GDP) 4.01 0.79% 1.17% 2.40% … R&D (business exp.) (perc. of GDP) 0.10 0.09% 0.17% 0.46%
entries.derivation: Value = the ETCR row's 5-year effect over its long-run effect, 0.72 ÷ 2.09 = 0.344 (derived; the plan's "about one-third"). Low = the slowest productivity row, business R&D, 0.09 ÷ 0.46 = 0.196; the openness row gives 0.79 ÷ 2.40 = 0.329. High = value (ETCR is the fastest).
entries.notes: Ratios of GDP-per-head effects, which mix MFP, K/Y and employment paths; applying them to a single channel's shock is an approximation. The paper's own path formula is in layer-b.ecm-mfp.eg2016.
